To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) IS is a powerful force in all languages, (ii) it is not limited to syntax, but affects all linguistic levels, including the phonetic, morphological and lexical level, (iii) the effects of IS on syntax are very different in different languages, and (iv) there are universal tendencies in the way IS is expressed in different languages.

(a) information structure is a powerful force in all levels of linguistic structure, (b) it is defined in terms of the communicative goals and the current attentional states of the interlocutor and (c) it is realized in a number of different ways in the different languages of the world.

(i) Information structure is a powerful force on linguistic form, (ii) information structure is not a single phenomenon but a set of related concepts, (iii) the different concepts are expressed in many ways in different languages, and (iv) the concepts are not independent, but interact with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which information structural functions are encoded, and with the effects that they exert on language structure, in particular on the syntax, morphology and phonology.

the following questions: What are the different information-structural functions? How are they expressed in languages? How do they interact with other structural phenomena? What are the cognitive and communicative principles that underly these phenomena?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IS is the packaging of information with the goal to optimize the form of a message to meet the immediate communicative goals.
the notion IS is a cover term for a variety of notional and formal distinctions.

information structure refers to those aspects of the form of an utterance that are determined by the immediate communicative need to satisfy the attentional state of the interlocutor, and which are not determined by the semantic and pragmatic content of the message itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

information structure is not a level of grammar but a set of notional distinctions, i.e. a set of functions, which may be realized in a variety of ways, and that the choice between these ways is motivated by the communicative context.
the information structural concepts of focus, givenness and topic, and the ways of expressing them, are the most fundamental and pervasive aspects of linguistic structure.

information structure is the set of linguistic means by which speakers package the information they wish to convey to their interlocutors in such a way as to optimize its processing and comprehension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information structure is a powerful force that exerts a strong influence on the structure of language and that it can be defined and investigated independently of any particular linguistic framework.
information structure has an effect on every level of linguistic structure.
IS is not just a feature that is added to a language, but that it exerts a powerful influence on the whole of the grammar.
